sentences.text: The only known fossil of this animal is a single, complete postcranial skeleton.
It possessed a very long neck with at least thirty-eight neck bones, a feature marked by unique small bumps on the front joints.
Scientists consider this creature one of the earliest known plesiosaurs.
Roger B. J. Benson, Mark Evans, and Patrick S. Druckenmiller first described and named the genus in 2012.
The specimen was found in Street, Watchet, Somerset, within the Pre-Planorbis beds of the Blue Lias Formation.
A 2012 study identified it as the most basal known plesiosauroid.
However, a later analysis by Benson and Druckenmiller in 2014 placed it as a basal plesiosaur outside the group Plesiosauroidea.
One estimate places its life between 199.6 and 198 million years ago during the earliest Hettangian stage.
Another record suggests a time range from 201.4 to 199.5 million years ago within the Hettangian stage.
